title: The win32 tarballs npm serves are not the bytes the CI candidate bundle recorded: CRLF in LICENSE and package.json
description: Reported by opum-cli-e2e with its TASK-106 receipt (opum-ai/opum-cli-e2e#242), 2026-09-25. It is relayed here and has not yet been re-measured in this repo. For quest 0.10.0, the candidate-bundle tarballs from run 35959762162 for quest-win32-x64 and quest-win32-arm64 differ from what npm serves only by CRLF line endings in LICENSE and package.json. The files are equal once CR is stripped, the executables are identical, and the other 5 of 7 tarballs match dist.integrity exactly. 0.9.0 has the same mismatch. Probable mechanism, not verified: the win32 package files are committed or checked out with CRLF (QCLI-347 recorded a 42-line LICENSE churn in npm/quest-win32-*), and the local publish packs the working-tree bytes rather than the CI bundle. Why it matters: any check binding a CI-bundle tarball digest to npm, including the receipt gate QCLI-366 will add, fails on these two packages. Not a 0.10.0 functional defect.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The mismatch is reproduced here by comparing the run 35959762162 candidate-bundle win32 tarball digests to npm dist.integrity for 0.10.0, and the root cause is named from evidence
The published win32 tarballs are byte-identical to the CI bundle for the next release, proven by the same comparison
A check fails the release when any published tarball differs from its CI-bundle digest

implementationNotes: Handoff 2026-09-25: not started. First step: download candidate-bundle from run 35959762162 and compare the win32 tarball sha512 against npm view @opum-ai/quest-win32-x64@0.10.0 dist.integrity. Then check git ls-files --eol npm/quest-win32-*/ for CRLF in the index versus the working tree.

REPRODUCED 2026-09-25 against the 0.10.0 candidate bundle from run 35959762162 and npm. dist.integrity: win32-x64 on npm sha512-30tV1Ta3lXag0eff2+600wTh3q37NKHIhzD2xbCRZPFBiX9pVzSR9xXRtojPylfpvbDdahuv3D8YSj3FBUt+2A==, bundle sha512-Jv/HBwcH8fbMtyHG40ZbySKx2ddb+RBueSuMUske4kut/RzV6z8pcfsfbAhFUwvEHn43wuBPAf+1TTQWOmJKEQ==. win32-arm64 on npm sha512-rDAo/q8xk6RdggzoyrEIpJt5uunWyuPGA8rQ7MnFHqAjOhkunA6JLPgw96NxzahcpYF9+lOkHezacWngSpDaCw==, bundle sha512-8HL7axIfKElYiR38Mk5SJgKonzQVYZA25+ChuOlVbOztheAjPVWiXRVw6gPhmzdBkPAxa2OWSgC78lhNT2UIww==. The other 5 of 7 packages match. ROOT CAUSE, correcting the relayed mechanism: the CRs are in the CI BUNDLE, not on npm. win32-x64 LICENSE and package.json carry 21 CRs each in the bundle and 0 in the npm tarball. Both files are 21 lines, so every line was converted, and the files are equal once CR is stripped. That is checkout-time core.autocrlf on the two Windows matrix legs (windows-2022, windows-11-arm): immutable-candidates uploads npm/quest-win32-* as checked out, and candidate-bundle packs it. The index and working tree here were already LF (git ls-files --eol: 12x i/lf w/lf). The local publish packed LF, so npm holds the LF bytes. FIX fd9b77e: .gitattributes pins npm/*/LICENSE and npm/*/package.json to text eol=lf, scoped narrowly so the darwin-arm64 binary is not re-examined (AMFI). Local pair via git -c core.autocrlf=true archive: origin/dev 21/21 CRs, fix 0/0. AC3: scripts/qualification/bundle-integrity.mjs compares npm dist.integrity for all 7 with the bundle files; both publishers run it after publishing and fail on any difference. Real negative control: run against 0.10.0 it exits 1 naming exactly the two win32 packages; the other five pass on real bytes. --verify-published could never have caught this because it compares only the executables. CI proof pending: workflow_dispatch run 36088520019 on fd9b77e; the expectation is a win32 bundle CR count of 0. AC2 needs the next release and is deferred to it.

CI PROOF (workflow_dispatch of prepublication-qualification on the fix branch). Run 36089487597 at 44f421d: every LICENSE and package.json in all 7 candidate-bundle tarballs has 0 CRs, win32-x64 and win32-arm64 included. NEGATIVE CONTROL, same workflow, one attribute line fewer: run 36088853907 at 6c387ba had win32 LICENSE 21 CRs and package.json 0. That run exposed a second source. Off a tag, build-platform-packages.mjs copies the ROOT LICENSE into every package and regenerates package.json with JSON.stringify, so the npm/* attributes did not govern that run at all; the root LICENSE is now pinned too (44f421d). Original control: the 0.10.0 tag bundle (run 35959762162) was 21/21. LIMIT, stated plainly: a branch dispatch exercises the rebuild path. The tag path, which packs npm/* exactly as checked out, runs only on a release tag, so its proof here is the local git -c core.autocrlf=true archive pair (21/21 before, 0/0 after) plus the next release, which is AC2. Also self-inflicted: the first dispatch (36088520019) was cancelled because I pushed to the branch mid-run and the concurrency group has cancel-in-progress. Dispatch only after the last push.
